intro_html: Cheese tortellini simmered in a creamy tomato sauce with browned turkey, spinach, and a heavy hand of parmesan. Each bowl delivers 31 grams of protein at 567 calories for about $4.15 (at everyday cost). The tortellini brings its own cheese filling to the party, so every bite eats rich.
cost_closing_html: About $4.15 a bowl (at everyday cost) for creamy tortellini with turkey. Any restaurant tortellini plate starts around $15 and goes up from there.
shop_smart: The tortellini is the splurge line here, and it is still what makes this dish possible. Watch for the refrigerated family-size bags on sale and stock the freezer.
Canned tomato sauce and a small can of paste build the sauce base for about $4. Jarred creamy tomato sauces of this volume would run $10 plus.
Frozen chopped spinach adds a vegetable for 83 cents. Nobody in the history of meal prep has regretted that purchase.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Season with salt, pepper, and half the Italian seasoning.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens a shade.
Add the tomato sauce, chicken broth, and remaining Italian seasoning. Bring to a simmer.
Add the tortellini and simmer 4 to 6 minutes, stirring gently, until they are tender and puffed.
Stir in the heavy cream and the thawed, squeezed-dry spinach and simmer 2 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and stir in most of the parmesan until melted.
Portion into 14 containers and dust with the remaining parmesan.
portion_html: Weigh the loaded pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scale that amount into each container. Each bowl finishes at about 567 calories with 31 grams of protein.

steps: Brown seasoned ground turkey in olive oil.
Cook garlic and tomato paste, then add tomato sauce and broth.
Simmer the tortellini right in the sauce until tender.
Stir in cream and spinach, then finish with parmesan off the heat.
